lead: Bleeding before 24 weeks. Miscarriage is the commonest cause, ectopic pregnancy the most dangerous, and molar pregnancy the one with very high hCG. Incidental causes: ectropion, polyp, cervicitis, cervical cancer.
f: Miscarriage: definition and types

Miscarriage: spontaneous loss before 24 wk; about 15–20% of known pregnancies · Threatened: mild bleeding, os closed, live fetus; most continue · Inevitable: heavy bleeding, colic, os open, nothing passed yet · Incomplete: os open, tissue in the os, uterus smaller than dates, may be shocked · Complete: pain and bleeding settle, os closed, empty uterus (exclude ectopic) · Missed: dead fetus retained, os closed, brown loss, symptoms fade · Septic: fever, offensive loss, tender uterus

sc: 10 wk, light bleed, os closed, live fetus on scan → Threatened miscarriage
Heavy bleed, colic, open os, nothing passed → Inevitable miscarriage

f: Aetiology

Chromosomal (aneuploidy): about 50% of first-trimester losses · Infection and high fever: malaria, TORCH · Endocrine: diabetes, thyroid disease, PCOS · Immune: antiphospholipid syndrome, SLE · Uterine anomaly, fibroid, cervical weakness · Drugs: quinine, alcohol, tobacco
Investigations

Speculum: os open or closed, local cause · FBC, blood group and Rh, malaria film · Transvaginal scan is the key test · Missed miscarriage: CRL ≥ 7 mm with no heartbeat, or mean sac ≥ 25 mm with no embryo · Confirm with a second opinion or a repeat scan ≥ 7 days later (NICE)
Management by type

Threatened: reassure; bed rest is unproven · Previous miscarriage + bleeding: vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily until 16 wk (NICE 2021) · Complete: confirm the empty uterus; pregnancy test negative after 2–3 wk · Inevitable, incomplete or missed: three options · Expectant: wait 2–4 wk; best under 8 wk · Medical: misoprostol; preferred from 12 wk · Surgical: MVA up to 12–14 wk; the choice for heavy bleeding, shock or sepsis

sc: Incomplete miscarriage, BP 80/50, heavy bleeding → Resuscitate, then evacuate (MVA)
tr: A missed miscarriage should not wait longer than 4 wk: a retained dead fetus can cause DIC

f: Misoprostol doses

Incomplete, under 13 wk: 600 µg oral or 400 µg sublingual once · Missed, under 13 wk: 800 µg vaginal or 600 µg sublingual; repeat after 3 h if needed · 13–24 wk: 400 µg sublingual or vaginal every 3 h · Priming before evacuation: 400 µg vaginal 3 h before, to soften the cervix
Surgical evacuation

MVA: plastic cannula and 60 mL hand syringe; no electricity; up to 12–14 wk under paracervical block · Prime the cervix first in a nullipara or near 12 wk · After 14 wk: D&E in theatre · Risks: bleeding, perforation, cervical tear, infection, Asherman syndrome, cervical weakness

tr: Amenorrhoea after repeated D&C → Asherman syndrome (intrauterine adhesions)

f: Septic miscarriage

Usually after an unsafe abortion or unclean instruments · Fever, rigors, offensive loss, tender uterus · Clostridium perfringens: haemolysis with jaundice and dark urine = severe sepsis · Complications: septic shock, AKI, DIC, ARDS, pelvic abscess, tubal block · Treat: resuscitate, cultures, ceftriaxone + metronidazole IV, anti-tetanus · Evacuate gently after antibiotics start (the soft uterus perforates easily)
Recurrent miscarriage

Definition: ≥ 3 miscarriages, not necessarily consecutive (RCOG 2023) · First trimester: antiphospholipid syndrome, parental translocation, PCOS, poorly controlled diabetes or thyroid disease · TORCH does not cause recurrent loss: do not test · Second trimester: cervical weakness (painless, each loss earlier), uterine anomaly (painful, each loss later), syphilis · Investigate: lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin twice, 12 wk apart, parental karyotype, pelvic scan, HbA1c, TSH · APS: aspirin 75 mg + enoxaparin 40 mg daily from a positive test · Cervical weakness: cerclage at 12–14 wk, removed at 36–37 wk or when labour starts

sc: 3 losses at 8–10 wk, lupus anticoagulant positive → Aspirin + LMWH in the next pregnancy
Painless second-trimester losses, each earlier than the last → Cervical weakness: cerclage

f: Anti-D in RhD-negative women

Miscarriage or ectopic: no anti-D before 12 wk (NICE 2025); from 12 wk 250 IU IM within 72 h · From 20 wk: 500 IU + Kleihauer test; 1500 IU if Kleihauer is not available · Local practice: often given after any loss from 10 wk, a partial mole or a surgical evacuation
Ectopic pregnancy

Implantation outside the uterine cavity; the ampulla of the tube is the commonest site · Positive hCG + empty uterus = ectopic until proven otherwise · Risk factors: PID, previous ectopic, tubal surgery, IUCD or progestogen-only pill, IVF, endometriosis · Features: amenorrhoea 6–8 wk, lower abdominal pain, dark spotting · Shoulder-tip pain, fainting: blood in the abdomen · Cervical excitation, adnexal mass
Ectopic: investigations

Transvaginal scan: empty uterus, adnexal mass, free fluid · An intrauterine sac should be seen once hCG is above about 2000 IU/L · Serial hCG 48 h apart: a viable pregnancy rises ≥ 35%; ectopic usually rises less, plateaus or falls slowly · Laparoscopy if still unclear · Differential: miscarriage, ovarian cyst accident, PID, appendicitis

tr: Never send home a woman with pain and a positive hCG before ectopic is excluded

f: Ectopic: treatment

Expectant: stable, little pain, hCG under 1000 and falling · Methotrexate 50 mg/m² IM: stable, hCG under 5000, mass under 3.5 cm, no heartbeat · Check hCG day 4 and day 7: success = day-7 level ≥ 15% lower than day 4; then weekly to negative · Surgery (laparoscopy): unstable, hCG over 5000, mass over 3.5 cm or live embryo · Salpingectomy if the other tube is healthy; salpingotomy if it is damaged (follow hCG) · Ruptured with shock: resuscitate and laparotomy now

sc: Pain, shock, fluid in the pelvis → Laparotomy now

f: Molar pregnancy (GTD)

Swollen villi and trophoblast overgrowth with very high hCG · Complete mole: empty ovum + sperm, 46,XX; no fetus; large for dates; malignant change about 15% · Partial mole: 69,XXY triploid; abnormal fetus; malignant change about 0.5% · Features: bleeding, grape-like vesicles, hyperemesis, pre-eclampsia before 20 wk, hyperthyroidism, theca lutein cysts · Scan: snowstorm, no fetus · Bloods: hCG, TFT; chest X-ray for lung spread

sc: BP 160/110 at 14 wk, uterus large for dates, no fetal heart → Complete mole

f: Molar pregnancy: management

Suction evacuation; no misoprostol before; oxytocin only once the uterus is emptying · Histology, then serial hCG until normal · No pregnancy until follow-up ends: condoms or the pill; no IUCD while hCG is raised · hCG plateau or rise = persistent GTN: FIGO score, methotrexate if ≤ 6 · Haemoptysis with rising hCG after a mole → choriocarcinoma
